description: Electorate figures where B. M. Walker's printed tables disagree with Civgraph. These records do NOT alter generated results: they are proposed corrections for review. Each was reached by extracting the figure from the scan, discarding any value that is the same seat's figure in another election or another seat's figure in the same election (both are row-bleed artefacts), and then reading the printed figure by eye. Vote figures were compared at the same time and are NOT listed: across roughly 585 vote comparisons every apparent disagreement failed Civgraph's own valid-poll reconciliation, marking it an OCR misread rather than an error in the data.

provenance.licence: Citations and figures only. Election results are facts and carry no copyright; the volumes themselves are in copyright, are not held in this repository, and no text from them is reproduced.
provenance.caveat: Three of these differ by 455 to 793 (Dublin County 1922, Waterford and Wexford 1923), which is too large for a transcription slip and may reflect a different electorate basis -- at dissolution versus at the poll -- rather than an error. Establish the basis before applying.

records.investigation: electionsireland.org gives 79,174 and states no basis; the Wikipedia constituency article repeats that figure and cites electionsireland, so it is one source twice, not a third. Valid poll and quota agree between the sources, so the difference is in the register figure alone. No official return exists to settle it: Walker states that official printed returns for Dail elections begin only with the Kerry South by-election of November 1944, and that for the general elections of 1922, 1923 and June 1927 local newspapers were the chief source. Both figures therefore most likely rest on contemporary newspaper reports. The remaining independent compilation is Gallagher, Irish Elections 1922-44 (1993). Until it is consulted Civgraph keeps its figure and the Walker figure is recorded here and shown beside the contest.
records.resolution: Gallagher gives 79,174, the figure Civgraph holds, so it stands and Walker's 78,381 is not adopted. Gallagher compiled every 1922-44 result from the provincial press, cross-checking papers against each other, and states that no official record of any pre-1948 general election exists; he treats Walker as a secondary compilation. electionsireland.org may itself draw on Gallagher, so this is agreement with the standard reference rather than a third independent count.

systematicGaps.finding: No electorate figure is held for any pre-1918 Westminster contest. Votes are complete at 96 of 96 in every election; electorate is empty in all of them. Figures first appear in 1922 (4 of 10) and are mostly present by 1950 (10 of 12).
systematicGaps.walkerSupplies: An elector count for every constituency, so roughly 860 figures across the nine elections.

systematicGaps.finding: Dublin University is absent entirely. It returned two members throughout the period.
Cork City is recorded as Number_Of_Seats "1" in every election while carrying 4 to 6 candidates. It returned two members.
systematicGaps.walkerSupplies: The page head states it: "Each constituency returns one M.P., except Cork city and Dublin University with two each." Corroborated by Wikipedia: 101 constituencies, 103 MPs.
